gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's 5kWh RV Kit, the 5,000 W kit Dealectric links that ships now, has a strict 50 V open-circuit limit on its solar input, so its panels must all be wired in parallel and never in series.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts' 5 kWh solar-input article (cited), StormWatts' same-panel-watts kit article and MachineFanatic's 5000W guide. StormWatts already has the port-by-port solar limits and panel wiring for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and Anker SOLIX S5000, including Jackery's two-panel cap on the SolarSaga 500 X, so that part of this angle is taken. None of the three mentions the BLUETTI RV5 kit, its 50 V limit, or that it is a wired-in system. None states that the S5000 does not work with Anker's Home Power Panel and takes only BP5000 batteries. MachineFanatic gives no volts, amps or connectors. solargenreview.com (cited) returned HTTP 429 and solargenadvisor.com a certificate error, so neither was read.
decides: It splits the answer by use rather than changing one winner. The BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit meets 5,000 W and ships now, but it is a 48 V system screwed and wired into an RV or van, with parallel-only panels under 50 V. It wins the RV/van-install segment, not the roll-it-out home-backup one. The portable 120/240 V answer, Jackery's Explorer 5000 Plus with 2× SolarSaga 500 X, was a pre-order on Jackery's store today (station ships Dec 2, panels by Dec 5). The Anker S5000 kit is 4,500 W, under the line, and cannot join a Home Power Panel. Anker's page for it also showed an 11–12 week ship window, which conflicts with the 'ships now' in the kits table and needs a re-check before it is named as a ships-now row.

findings.label: Solar input voltage limit
findings.value: 50 V open-circuit (Voc) maximum on the PV input
findings.source_title: A Deep Dive into the BLUETTI RV5 48V DIY Solar Inverter Kit (BLUETTI US)
findings.note: BLUETTI's wording: 'The RV5 has a strict 50V VOC (Voltage Open Circuit) limit on the PV input.' It adds that standard residential panels, often 60–80 V Voc, 'WILL destroy the charge controller if connected directly.'

findings.label: Panel wiring rule
findings.source_title: A Deep Dive into the BLUETTI RV5 48V DIY Solar Inverter Kit (BLUETTI US)
findings.note: BLUETTI's wording: 'all panels MUST be wired in PARALLEL, never in series.' It recommends high-amp Y-branch adapters and 6-gauge cabling, and names the PV100 FX as the parallel-ready panel.

findings.label: Alternator charging through PV2
findings.source_title: A Deep Dive into the BLUETTI RV5 48V DIY Solar Inverter Kit (BLUETTI US)
findings.note: The PV2 input doubles as the alternator charger, so a solar array on PV2 shares that input with the alternator. The guide gives the B4810 as 51.2 V, 100 Ah, 5,120 Wh and says the Edock box 'allows for the integration of third-party 48V batteries.'

findings.label: AC output and what kind of product it is
findings.value: 5,000 W continuous, 10,000 W surge; a system mounted and wired into the vehicle, not a portable station
findings.note: The box list includes 8 M8 wood screws, 8 anchors, a drilling template, and battery, alternator-charger and distribution-panel wiring packs. The FAQ says 'no electrician required.' The page also lists total load 6,000 W max and DC output 1,620 W. Its spec table did not load, so no AC voltage was read.
